terms.gloss: throat, the back of the mouth
evidence: Plin. NH 11.179: summum gulae faucēs vocantur (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The everyday word for the throat as it gets sore, dry or hoarse; plural in prose (the singular fauce is poetic). Also the narrow entrance of anything, a pass or a gorge (see gorge).

evidence: Ov. Am. 1.13.8: liquidum tenuī gutture cantat avis (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The gullet and the throat from outside, as a bird sings with it or a goitre swells in it; also, by transfer, gluttony (Juv. 2.114). Lewis & Short marks it chiefly ante-classical and poetic.
The gullet, the passage food goes down; much more often greed for food (gulae parēre, Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: caret ōs ūmōre loquentis et faucēs ārent, vixque est via vōcis in illīs
phrases.english: my mouth is dry as I speak, my throat is parched, and there is hardly a way through it for my voice

phrases.latin: obstipuī, steteruntque comae et vōx faucibus haesit
phrases.english: I froze, my hair stood on end and my voice stuck in my throat
